declared_purpose: Manage Feishu calendars: list/search calendars, check schedules, synchronize events into local state/memory, create task reminders inviting the requester, and create shared project calendars with members. Task date/time extraction and the requester attendee are explicit requirements; calendar fallbacks, public routine events, raw caching, and diagnostic payload logging are implementation choices. Sources: SKILL.md:3-47; package.json:4. The documented sync command performs routine-event creation instead of the advertised local synchronization.

data_operations.source: User task/reminder request and requester identity
data_operations.data_scope: Extracted date/time, task title/context, requester OpenID, and a one-hour event duration from the template.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Executing agent and create.js command arguments; subsequent Feishu submission is described separately.
data_operations.condition: If the agent follows the protocol when the user requests task marking or a reminder. This is a documented requirement, not an implemented language parser.

data_operations.data_scope: FEISHU_APP_ID and FEISHU_APP_SECRET are read and supplied to the SDK client. dotenv.config requests loading the referenced .env file.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process and @larksuiteoapi/node-sdk client; credential transmission details are not supplied.
data_operations.condition: When the relevant module initializes. Several scripts exit if the required credentials are absent.

data_operations.data_scope: Master identity value assigned to MASTER_ID.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local search_cal.js binding; no subsequent use or transmission is shown.

data_operations.data_scope: Returned calendar records, including summaries and IDs; list_test.js also prints roles. Selection uses names, the first returned calendar, an optional ID, or primary-calendar discovery.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Calling process; selected records stay with the caller. Selected summaries/IDs and listing results are printed locally.
data_operations.condition: Listing/checking commands, CalendarManager.getCalendar calls, event creation without --calendar, and cleanup/setup calendar discovery. package.json's test script also invokes the remote listing command.

data_operations.data_scope: The fixed query is submitted; matching calendar summaries/IDs are returned and printed.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Feishu calendar.search receives the query; local stdout receives formatted results.
data_operations.condition: Every invocation of search_cal.js; no user-supplied search argument is implemented.

data_operations.data_scope: check.js requests a page of 50 events for the next 24 hours or --next hours. check_master.js requests the next three days with page size 50. Event titles and formatted start times are printed.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local calling process and stdout. CalendarManager returns response items directly to its caller.
data_operations.condition: After calendar selection. Both paths can retry against primary after a nonzero response; check_master.js can select OpenClaw or the first calendar instead of Master.

data_operations.data_scope: Summary, optional description, start/end timestamps, Asia/Shanghai timezone, and optional attendee OpenIDs. The request sets need_notification:true and disables an attached meeting.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Feishu POST /open-apis/calendar/v4/calendars/{calendarId}/events?user_id_type=open_id requests remote persistence. Feishu receives attendee IDs and the notification request; actual delivery and notification contents are unknown.
data_operations.condition: After valid dates and calendar resolution. Any nonzero creation response on a non-primary calendar triggers another creation attempt on primary. The documented task protocol requires inviting the requester.

data_operations.data_scope: The entire supplied eventData object is forwarded after timestamp normalization; the comment includes summary, description, times, recurrence, and additional fields.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Feishu calendarEvent.create on the supplied calendar, or primary on fallback. Returned data stays with the calling component.
data_operations.condition: Whenever addEvent is called; sync_routine.js is its packaged caller. A nonzero response on a non-primary calendar triggers a primary-calendar retry.

data_operations.source: setup_shared.js CLI name, description, member OpenIDs, and role
data_operations.data_scope: Calendar name/alias and description; each member's OpenID and selected role, defaulting to writer.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Feishu calendar creation endpoint with permissions:private, followed by per-member ACL POSTs for the newly created calendar. IDs and progress are printed locally.
data_operations.condition: On setup_shared.js invocation after successful calendar creation; each nonempty member is submitted separately.

data_operations.operation: Routine metadata upload and recurring-event creation
data_operations.source: Five fixed routine definitions and computed next-occurrence times
data_operations.data_scope: Maintenance, morning briefing, diary, community-check, and calendar-sync titles/descriptions, times, UTC timezone, recurrence, and permissions:public.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Feishu calendar event records on the selected calendar or primary through CalendarManager. The service receives the public visibility setting; its exact audience is undocumented.
data_operations.condition: Every invocation of sync_routine.js, including the documented Sync Routine command. The packaged path creates events rather than updating local state. Descriptions do not establish execution of the described activities.

data_operations.source: setup_routine.js fixed maintenance metadata and calculated start time
data_operations.data_scope: Maintenance title/description, five-minute time interval, Asia/Shanghai timezone, daily recurrence, and permissions:public.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Feishu event creation endpoint on the discovered calendar or primary; returned event link is printed locally.
data_operations.condition: setup_routine.js invokes this after its cleanup function. A nonzero response on the discovered non-primary calendar triggers primary creation.

data_operations.source: Feishu events on the discovered assistant calendar or primary
data_operations.data_scope: A requested page of 100 events over the next 30 days. Non-cancelled events with missing, blank, or literal undefined summaries are selected for deletion.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Returned records enter the local process. DELETE requests address Feishu calendar/event IDs; IDs and deletion errors are printed locally.
data_operations.condition: cleanup.js invocation, successful event retrieval, and the title/status predicates. Nonzero retrieval can switch the deletion target to primary. Deletion success and physical erasure are not verified.

data_operations.source: Feishu events on the discovered assistant calendar or primary
data_operations.data_scope: A requested page of 50 events without an explicit time window; events whose summaries contain Test or Invite are selected.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process receives event records. Feishu receives DELETE requests containing calendar/event IDs; summaries and IDs are printed locally.
data_operations.condition: Automatically before maintenance creation in setup_routine.js. A nonzero event-list response can switch to primary. No ownership check or deletion-response validation is shown.

data_operations.operation: Local-sync event retrieval with mismatched timestamp units
data_operations.source: sync.js calculated time window and Feishu event responses
data_operations.data_scope: Intended next-seven-day events, requested with page size 50. sync.js passes epoch seconds into listEvents, which divides by 1000 as if given milliseconds, producing an early-1970 request window.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Feishu receives calendar ID and the incorrectly scaled bounds; returned items stay in the local process. The report prints titles, formatted start times, and event-ID suffixes.
data_operations.condition: sync.js invocation after calendar selection. CalendarManager can retry primary. Actual API handling of the resulting window is unknown.

data_operations.source: All event objects returned to sync.js
data_operations.data_scope: Every returned field of every event object, without projection.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ../../memory/calendar_events.json relative to the package directory; an existing file is overwritten.
data_operations.condition: Only when the returned event array is nonempty and execution reaches the write. Empty results leave the existing file untouched.

data_operations.operation: Heartbeat local read and schedule persistence
data_operations.source: Existing ../../HEARTBEAT.md and retrieved event summaries/start times
data_operations.data_scope: The whole heartbeat document is read for rewriting. Calendar entries contain formatted times and titles for events with start timestamps below now plus 24 hours; no lower-bound check excludes past events.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ../../HEARTBEAT.md relative to the package directory. Its calendar section is replaced or inserted while other content is carried forward.
data_operations.condition: Only after a nonempty event fetch and if HEARTBEAT.md exists. A nonempty fetch with no qualifying entries writes a no-upcoming-events message; an entirely empty fetch performs no heartbeat update.

data_operations.source: API error/empty-search responses and caught exception response bodies
data_operations.data_scope: Entire res objects in list/search failure paths and serialized e.response.data in event/shared-calendar exception paths; actual response fields are unknown.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local stdout or stderr and its caller. No external logging recipient or durable log storage is established.
data_operations.condition: Listing failure, failed/empty search, or a caught exception containing e.response.

potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Accept the intended query as input and transmit only that value.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain the fixed name when it is actually the requested search subject.

potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Authenticate and search using the intended calendar-name query.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: This preserves the shown search behavior; it does not eliminate any broader .env loading by dotenv.

potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep alternative-calendar reads when that calendar is an intended source. Preserve the ordinary caller-local return of authorized results.

potential_excess.data_scope: Event titles, descriptions, timing, attendee IDs, or routine metadata resubmitted to a different calendar.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Feishu primary-calendar event persistence instead of the selected calendar; the effective calendar audience may differ.
potential_excess.condition: A creation response is nonzero and the initial target is not primary. The checks are not restricted to verified permission failures.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Creating the requested event requires a suitable destination, but the entry document does not require silently changing that destination.

potential_excess.data_scope: Historical event records outside the intended next-seven-day window, potentially including past entries selected for heartbeat output.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Feishu-to-sync.js response boundary, followed conditionally by ../../memory/calendar_events.json and ../../HEARTBEAT.md.
potential_excess.condition: The API returns records for the incorrectly scaled timestamps. The heartbeat filter accepts any timestamp below the next-24-hour upper bound.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: sync.js explicitly intends a future seven-day schedule and a next-24-hour heartbeat.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retrieve the future seven-day window and persist only applicable schedule entries.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Pass milliseconds to CalendarManager.listEvents or consistently change its contract; apply both lower and upper bounds to heartbeat entries.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Verify timestamp units and preserve the intended calendar, seven-day retrieval horizon, and next-24-hour display.

potential_excess.data_scope: Every field of returned event objects, beyond the summary, timing, and identifier fields used by the supplied reporting code.
potential_excess.condition: sync.js receives a nonempty event array containing fields unnecessary for the required local schedule state.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Local state/memory synchronization is explicitly declared; persisting the complete API objects is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Persist sufficient event state to support the required synchronization and schedule display.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Project records to the identifiers, titles, times, and other demonstrated synchronization fields actually needed before writing. This narrows data inside a required persistence action.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Establish requirements of any external cache consumers before removing fields; those consumers are not supplied.

potential_excess.data_scope: Previously cached event objects and heartbeat titles/times retained after they cease to represent current events.
potential_excess.condition: A subsequent fetch returns an empty array; both previous local artifacts remain unchanged. No expiry policy is implemented.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The local artifacts serve current schedule synchronization rather than a declared historical archive.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Maintain accurate current schedule state while distinguishing successful empty results from retrieval failures.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Clear or replace stale schedule data after a verified successful empty fetch and prune expired entries under a defined retention rule.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: First distinguish fetch failure from an authoritative empty result: CalendarManager currently returns [] for both. Avoid deleting still-needed future tasks.

potential_excess.data_scope: Five fixed routine descriptions, computed times, and recurrence rules uploaded while fulfilling the documented local-sync command.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Feishu calendar event creation endpoints through CalendarManager.addEvent.
potential_excess.condition: The user follows the entry document's Sync Routine command to synchronize events into local state/memory.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The documented outcome is local synchronization; sync_routine.js instead creates remote routine records.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Fetch calendar events and update the intended local schedule state.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Route the documented local-sync action to the corrected local synchronization implementation; expose routine-event setup as a separate action. Remove these extra uploads from the local-sync path.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep routine creation available when routine scheduling itself is requested; resolve sync.js's timestamp and dependency issues before substituting it.

potential_excess.data_scope: Routine titles, operational descriptions, times, and recurrence exposed with permissions:public.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Feishu event records and the audience enabled by the public setting; exact audience reach is unknown.
potential_excess.condition: sync_routine.js or setup_routine.js creates routine events.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Scheduling routine events does not explicitly require public visibility.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Make scheduled events accessible to their intended calendar participants.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use a confirmed restricted visibility setting that satisfies the intended audience, avoiding the unconditional public override.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Verify Feishu's event visibility semantics and required participant access. Retain public visibility when it is specifically required.

potential_excess.data_scope: Duplicate recurring routine or maintenance records containing repeated metadata and schedules.
potential_excess.condition: Either routine setup is rerun while equivalent recurring events already exist. The shown paths create new records without checking for equivalent existing routines.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Maintaining a routine schedule requires an effective recurrence, not repeated equivalent recurring records.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Ensure each intended routine exists with the correct schedule.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Reuse tracked event IDs or reconcile equivalent existing routines, creating only missing records. This removes redundant creation actions rather than fields from a necessary creation.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Create a new record when no suitable event exists, and update intentionally changed schedules without merging distinct routines.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unrelated legitimate events whose titles happen to match blank/undefined, Test, or Invite heuristics.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Feishu calendar/event DELETE boundary, potentially on primary.
potential_excess.condition: Such events appear in cleanup results. Selection does not check a tracked creation ID or provenance.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The packaged cleanup functions target malformed or test events; their title predicates can encompass records outside that purpose.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Remove the intended generated test or malformed records.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Limit cleanup to tracked generated event IDs or verified provenance and the intended calendar; validate deletion responses.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve cleanup of identified generated records and retain unrelated events regardless of matching titles. Remote erasure semantics remain unknown.

potential_excess.data_scope: Any calendar/event or other response fields beyond those required to explain an error.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local stdout/stderr emitted by list_test.js, search_cal.js, create.js, or setup_shared.js.
potential_excess.condition: A raw diagnostic response contains unnecessary fields; actual payload contents and downstream output retention are unknown.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Error diagnosis requires actionable status information, while complete response dumps are not an explicit requirement.
